issues.description: setuptools<82 pin leaks a CI build constraint into core/setup.py's runtime install_requires.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flag this as the central issue: capping setuptools in install_requires conflates a build-time CI workaround for mmcv with the library's runtime contract, propagating the ceiling to every downstream user of the hyperopt extra. The constraint belongs in CI workflow files or pyproject build-system requires, not the package's runtime dependency list.

issues.description: Three duplicated setuptools<82 pins with no single source of truth or shared revert spec.
issues.detail: env_setup.sh, setup_mmcv.sh, and core/setup.py each independently assert setuptools<82, with FIXME comments inconsistently applied. When upstream mmcv#3325 resolves, the operator must remember all three sites. No shared constant, script, or documented invariant ties them together, inviting silent drift.

issues.description: Silent mmdet 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 bump (and mmengine SHA to 0.10.7) bundled into a CI fix.
issues.detail: The PR ostensibly fixes mmengine setuptools failures but also bumps mmdet a minor version and replaces a torch-2.5-compat mmengine SHA pin with PyPI 0.10.7. No justification is given that 0.10.7 preserves the prior torch-2.5 invariant. Bundling unrelated version changes under one CI patch hurts bisectability.

issues.description: --no-build-isolation on mmcv silently couples the build to ambient environment state.
issues.detail: Disabling build isolation means mmcv's build now reads whatever setuptools/wheel/torch the active env provides instead of the isolated PEP 517 contract. It works only because the previous line pre-pins setuptools<82, an implicit and brittle invariant. A short inline comment explaining why isolation is disabled would help the next maintainer.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously views this as a pragmatic CI hotfix that mostly does the right thing in shell scripts but leaks a build-time constraint into the library's runtime contract. The central P1 concern, flagged by all three reviewers, is that setuptools<82 in core/setup.py's install_requires propagates a CI workaround to every downstream user. The second P1 is that the same pin lives in three locations with no shared source of truth, making the eventual revert fragile. Secondary issues are an unjustified mmdet/mmengine version bump riding along under the setuptools fix, and --no-build-isolation implicitly coupling mmcv's build to ambient env state. No architectural rework needed — this is contract-hygiene cleanup on a hotfix.
